solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Helps gullible people, you say?

indicators.note: the question 'you say?' tells the solver the word is to be spoken, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: suckers are people easily fooled

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether helping others is just for the easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is an old verb for giving aid, so 'helps' matches its third-person form.

clue.text: Only one flatfish

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective meaning single or the one and only
Dover ... is a well-known flat sea fish

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the adjective meaning single; the other is a species of flat fish.

clue.text: Such inspiring call from family about Brazilian port

indicators.note: the family word goes around the port, enclosing it

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group
Rio de Janeiro is Brazil's famous port city

explanation.surface: Relatives gather to rally round a Brazilian harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarion call is a rousing summons, after the clear-toned trumpet once used in war.

clue.text: Learner in their hovel, dilapidated, past best

indicators.note: a dilapidated building is falling apart, so these letters are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate in Britain

explanation.surface: A learner driver lives in a family's rundown shack that has seen better days.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes 'in' with THEIR HOVEL and all those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for someone too old to be at their peak, beyond their prime.

clue.text: In thesaurus setter finding name of apple

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler looks up a fruit variety in a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a family of apple varieties with rough brownish skin, such as Egremont Russet.

clue.text: Photo on Net? Impressive!

indicators.note: in this clue 'on' says the photo piece is attached after the net piece

parts.note: E is the prefix for things electronic or online, as in e-mail
a pic is a casual word for a photo

explanation.surface: Someone sees a picture posted online and exclaims at how impressive it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is informal praise for anything grand or remarkable, a near synonym of impressive.

clue.text: Criticise extremely taboo stage show

parts.note: to pan is to review harshly

indicators.note: at its extremes, only the first and last letters of taboo are used

explanation.surface: A reviewer slates a theatre production for being far too risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for pantomime, a British comic family theatre show staged around Christmas.

clue.text: Charlie near bar, rebuilt, in capital city

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie stands near a pub that was reconstructed in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the purpose-built capital of Australia.

clue.text: Abandon holiday

definitions.meaning: to walk away from and desert someone or something
time off work granted by an employer

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: departing from something, and permitted time away from duty.

clue.text: Quiet girl on Irish river

parts.note: sh is the sound used to ask for silence
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A shy young woman is pictured beside a river in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland, flowing to the Atlantic near Limerick.

clue.text: A cadet's air I blasted sailing here?

indicators.note: blasted means blown apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A naval trainee's tune is blown out while at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans, a place a cadet might sail.

clue.text: Rock hero given to playing well

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: A rock music star, devoted to performing, is doing it brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre but is the anagram signal working on HERO GIVEN TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for performing smoothly and confidently, especially of musicians or sportspeople on form.

clue.text: Rich, a female speaking foreign language well

parts.note: someone fluent speaks a language easily

explanation.surface: A wealthy woman is also a gifted linguist.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent is a synonym for wealthy, describing people with plenty of money.

clue.text: Criminal dealer meets resistance fighter

parts.note: a fence is someone who trades in stolen goods
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A crook who handles stolen goods comes up against a member of an underground movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman in the sport of fencing is a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Clergyman's previous life with ordinary soldiers

definitions.note: read as 'clergyman is', with the 's as a link to the wordplay

parts.note: one's past is one's earlier life
OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A vicar's earlier career was spent serving among the rank-and-file troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, a kind of clergyman.

clue.text: One complaining in distinctive voice seeing capacity of ship

indicators.note: the complainer word is placed inside the voice word

parts.note: a tone is a characteristic quality of voice
a nag is someone who complains persistently

explanation.surface: A grumbler with an unmistakable voice is seen aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage measures a vessel's size or cargo-carrying volume.

clue.text: Addition not meant, we hear, to be flexible

indicators.note: not means the following piece is removed from the addition word

parts.note: a supplement is something added

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver only the sound of the word meant is used

parts.note: pronounced like the word ending -ment

explanation.surface: An extra that was never intended has to bend to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPLEMENT loses the ending that sounds like 'meant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple describes something that bends easily, a direct synonym of flexible.

clue.text: It's small, wobbly — I'll nail it up

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and shaken, so these letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: Someone notes a little shelf is unsteady and promises to fix it to the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link before the definition; 'wobbly' rearranges I'LL NAIL IT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: From the tiny people of Lilliput in Gulliver's Travels, the word means very little or petty.

clue.text: The French versus the Spanish, with neither side leading?

parts.note: le is French for the
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: France plays Spain, and the scores are tied.
explanation.definitionFit: When scores are equal, the contest is drawn and nobody is ahead.

clue.text: Right to interrupt indulged person, impudent

indicators.note: the right letter breaks into the middle of the word for a favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite who is spoiled

explanation.surface: A spoiled child cuts in with cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Pert means cheeky or saucy, a synonym of impudent.

clue.text: Envy, no end, returning Pole's wrap

indicators.note: with no end means the word's final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: returning means the word for the Polish person is written backwards

parts.note: a person from Poland, taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A jealous Polish person's wrap is being admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims ENVY to ENV; 'returning' turns POLE into ELOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to surround or cover completely, a synonym of wrap as a verb.

clue.text: From Treviso, a very Italian wine

indicators.note: letters taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A bottle from the town of Treviso is described as very Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto region of north-east Italy.

clue.text: Had impact at first that one loved dearly

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following four words is taken

explanation.surface: A sentimental remark about how much a cherished person mattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has told on a person has had a marked effect, as in 'the strain told'.

clue.text: Ten years associated with heartless nest, corrupt

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outer letters of the word nest remain

explanation.surface: A decade spent in a cold, uncaring home leaves someone morally rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline and self-indulgence, close in sense to corrupt.
